note: Source manifest for the ORCH-753 gold cohort. The paper text is NOT committed; it lives at C:/t/eval-fulltext/<PMCID>.txt and gold.load_fulltext refuses a text whose sha256 differs.
citation: Schedlbauer A et al. Aminolevulinate inhibition of human coproporphyrinogen oxidase clarifies coproporphyrin III accumulation in porphyrias Bioscience reports 2026.
pathway_in_one_line: Why coproporphyrin III piles up in ALAD-deficiency porphyria: accumulated delta-aminolevulinic acid inhibits coproporphyrinogen oxidase, and the oxidised substrate coproporphyrin III inhibits it further.
scope_note: In scope: 2 delta-aminolevulinic acid -> porphobilinogen (ALAD, the deficient enzyme), coproporphyrinogen III -> protoporphyrinogen IX (CPOX, oxidative decarboxylation, the reaction assayed here), the non-enzymatic oxidation coproporphyrinogen III -> coproporphyrin III, and the chemical hydrogenation coproporphyrin III -> coproporphyrinogen III used to prepare substrate. Also stated: succinylacetoacetate/maleylacetoacetate decomposing to succinylacetone in tyrosinemia type I. Adjacent: the rest of the heme pathway, the inhibition kinetics and Michaelis-Menten parameters (not conversions), the lead inactivation result, and the circular-dichroism/thermal-stability characterisation. Note the distinction the paper itself insists on: coproporphyrin III is a non-enzymatic by-product, not a physiological reaction product - an extraction that books it as the CPOX product is wrong even though the two names are near-identical.
selected_because: The shortest paper in the set (44k chars) and the only one whose content is a human disease mechanism carried by explicit chemistry, so it fills a content cell and an organism cell at once. The porphyrinogen-vs-porphyrin pair is a hard, biologically real naming test. It also deliberately separates an enzymatic product from a chemical by-product, which the product contract cares about and which no current gold paper exercises.
